The '''Chiggnash''', sometimes refered to as '''Chiggers''', were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] with [[Color/Legends|yellow]] carapaces and [[Scorpion/Legends|scorpionic]] bodies. The species was able to [[Control Mind (Chiggnash)|control the minds]] of other beings after injecting them with a serum from their [[Meter/Legends|meter]]&ndash;long stingers. This ability allowed Chiggnash's to rapidly accumulate an expendable force of [[warrior drone]]s which required special tactics to deal with. However the effect could be counteracted within the first six [[Standard day/Legends|days]]. 

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the Chiggnash criminals [[Riley (Chiggnash)|Riley]] and [[Banda (Chiggnash)|Banda]] operated an extortion ring on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shadda]]. However the pair were [[Death/Legends|killed]] after trying to rob [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Squib_tensor_rifle.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Chiggnash were able to hold tensor rifles (pictured) in their dexterous pincers]]
Chiggnashs were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Scorpion/Legends|scorpion]]&ndash;like [[Spider/Legends|arachnoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]] with a multi&ndash;segmented carapace, four spiking hind [[Limb/Legends|legs]], and triangular heads that lacked discernible [[eye]]s. Their carapaces were [[Color/Legends|yellow]] and could include small brown spots. Jutting from their long torsos were a pair of thicker arms that included a set of pincers that were dexterous enough to grasp [[tensor rifle]]s. Two cudgel&ndash;like [[Claw/Legends|claws]] extended from their chunky forearms and they had skinny harpoon&ndash;tails that could coil.<ref name="Lone Wolf" /> 

Chiggnashs were able to use their [[Meter/Legends|meter]]&ndash;long stingers to inject other sentient species with a serum that allowed the Chiggnash to [[Control Mind (Chiggnash)|control the minds]] of their victim. If the venom inside these [[warrior drone]]s was not counteracted during the next six [[Standard day/Legends|days]] the being would end up in a permanent vegetative state.<ref name="Lone Wolf" />

==History==
By [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="Lone Wolf Date">The events of "[[Lone Wolf: A Tale of Obi-Wan and Luke]]" occur during those of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], which ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].</ref> the exact [[Pheromone/Legends|pheromone]] bedrock of how the Chiggnash zombifying serum worked on [[Alien/Legends|alien]] physiologies were debated by [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologists]].<ref name="Lone Wolf" /> Among [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]], it was acknowledged that due to their mind control ability, special tactics were required to confront Chiggnash. For instance, an electrified [[smart-harpoon]] was considered an inappropriate weapon as it would soon short out against the many warrior drones that a Chiggnash could bring to bear. Similarly, a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] was considered to only be a temporary solution against their drone hordes.<ref name="Predators of the Empire" />

==Chiggnash in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Hand over the credits, outlander.|The Chiggnash Banda, to Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Lone Wolf" />}}
[[File:Nar_Shaddaa_LoNH.png|thumb|right|200px|The Chiggnash Riley and Banda operated on the moon Nar Shadda (pictured).]]
Chiggnash were sometimes referred to Chiggers by other beings in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and were known as professional kidnappers, blackmailers, and [[Slavery/Legends|enslavers]].<ref name="Lone Wolf" /> At least some Chiggnash formed criminal extortion rings.<ref name="Predators of the Empire" /> By 19 [['ABY-BBY' dating system/Legends|BBY]],<ref name="Lone Wolf Date" /> the Chiggnash criminals [[Riley (Chiggnash)|Riley]] and [[Banda (Chiggnash)|Banda]] were active on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler's]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]].<ref name="Lone Wolf" /> 

That [[Standard year/Legends|year]],<ref name="Lone Wolf Date" /> the pair worked with [[Shnozitskigante-maximilliana]], a [[Pacithhip/Legends|Pacithhip]] [[Hangar/Legends|docking bay]] attendant, to try to rob the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. When they confronted Kenobi with tensor rifles and a force of warrior drones made up of [[Kyuzo/Legends|Kyuzos]] and [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]], the Chiggnash were instead cut down by the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Mei (Dark Jedi)|Mei]].<ref name="Lone Wolf" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Your electrified smart-harpoon ''[is]'' hardly the weapon of choice for going up against a Chiggnash extortion ring. After all, the Control Mind of the scorpion-like Chiggnash breeds warrior drones like a termite queen lays eggs.|Advice for confronting Chiggnash from Predators of the Empire|<ref name="Predators of the Empire" />}}
Chiggnash were first mentioned in "[[Predators of the Empire]]," an article written by [[Brian Daley]] and published in the [[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine 6|sixth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine]]''<ref name="Predators of the Empire" /> in [[January]] [[1996]].<ref name="Galaxy Magazine 6 Date">[[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine 6|''Star Wars Galaxy Magazine'' 6]] states that the [[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine]] was published quarterly and that it was released in winter [[1996]]. Since [[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine 7|''Star Wars Galaxy Magazine'' 7]] states that it was released in [[April]] of 1996, issue 6 must have been published in [[January]] 1996.</ref> The article was written in a mix of both [[In-universe]] and Out-of-Universe perspective.<ref name="Predators of the Empire" /> The species later appeared in the short story "[[Lone Wolf: A Tale of Obi-Wan and Luke]]," where they were also first referred to as Chiggers by one character. The story was written by [[Abel G. Peña]]<ref name="Lone Wolf" /> and published to [[StarWars.com]] on [[March 6]], [[2015]] as part of the [[SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story]] novella.<ref name="LostMissions">{{SW|url=news/the-other-lost-missions-rare-clone-wars-comics-and-literature-part-2|text=The Other Lost Missions: Rare Clone Wars Comics and Literature, Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref>
